name: Alfa Romeo 158
notes: The 'Alfetta' dominated the first official World Championship season, winning every round it entered.

name: Ferrari 500
notes: Alberto Ascari's car for two consecutive titles, in a period when the championship ran to Formula 2 rules.

name: Mercedes-Benz W196
notes: Streamlined and desmodromic-valved, it carried Juan Manuel Fangio to titles in 1954 and 1955.

name: Cooper T51
notes: The rear-engined layout that changed Formula 1 for good.

name: Lotus 49
notes: Debuted the legendary Cosworth DFV as a stressed member of the chassis and won on its first race.

name: Lotus 72
notes: Wedge-shaped, with side radiators and inboard brakes; raced in several forms until 1975.

name: McLaren M23
notes: Won titles for Emerson Fittipaldi in 1974 and James Hunt in 1976.

name: Ferrari 312T
notes: The transverse gearbox ('T') gave better weight distribution and carried Niki Lauda to the 1975 title.

name: Lotus 79
notes: Perfected ground-effect aerodynamics, with sculpted sidepods acting as inverted wings.

name: Williams FW07
notes: A ground-effect design that gave Williams its first wins and, in FW07B form, the 1980 title.

name: McLaren MP4/4
notes: Won 15 of 16 races in 1988 with Ayrton Senna and Alain Prost.

name: Williams FW14B
notes: Active suspension and traction control made it the most advanced car of its day.

name: Ferrari F2004
notes: Won 15 of 18 races in 2004 and is widely considered one of the most dominant cars ever.

name: Brawn BGP 001
notes: Built on a shoestring budget with a double diffuser, and won the title in the team's only season.

name: Mercedes-AMG F1 W11 EQ Performance
notes: Featured Dual-Axis Steering (DAS) and won the title for the seventh straight year.

name: Red Bull RB19
notes: Won 21 of 22 races in 2023, the highest win rate in a single season.

name: McLaren MCL39
notes: Carried Lando Norris to the 2025 championship.
